problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.summary: Given a grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water), count the islands. Land cells belong to the same island when they touch up, down, left or right.
problems.idea: For each unvisited '1', count it and flood-fill (BFS/DFS) its island to mark visited. O(m·n).
problems.topics: Array, Depth-First Search, Breadth-First Search, Union-Find, Matrix

problems.title: Nested List Weight Sum II
problems.summary: You get a nested list of integers. An integer's weight is maxDepth − depth + 1, so the deepest integers weigh 1 and top-level ones weigh the most. Return the sum of every integer times its weight.
problems.idea: BFS level by level; keep a running sum of all integers seen so far and add it to the total at each level — deeper items get counted fewer times.

class NestedInteger:
    """Provided: isInteger(), getInteger(), getList()."""
    def __init__(self, v): self._v = v
    def isInteger(self) -> bool: return isinstance(self._v, int)
    def getInteger(self): return self._v if isinstance(self._v, int) else None
    def getList(self): return self._v if isinstance(self._v, list) else None

problems.title: Max Stack
problems.summary: Design a stack that also supports finding and removing its maximum: push(x), pop(), top(), peekMax(), and popMax(). If several elements share the max, popMax removes the one closest to the top.
problems.example: push 5, push 1, push 5 → top()=5, popMax()=5, top()=1, peekMax()=5, pop()=1, top()=5
problems.idea: Doubly linked list for stack order + TreeMap<val, Deque<Node>> for max; popMax unlinks from the middle. O(log n).
problems.topics: Linked List, Stack, Design, Doubly-Linked List, Ordered Set

problems.title: Can Place Flowers
problems.summary: A flowerbed is an array of 0 (empty) and 1 (planted). Flowers can't be planted in adjacent plots. Return whether n more flowers can be planted.
problems.example: flowerbed [0,0,1,0,0], n = 2 → true (plant at both ends)
problems.idea: Greedy: plant whenever the current, left and right plots are empty (out of bounds = empty).

problems.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number

problems.example: "23" → [ad, ae, af, bd, be, bf, cd, ce, cf]
problems.idea: Backtrack digit by digit, append each mapped letter, undo.

problems.title: Decode String

problems.idea: Stack of (repeat count, string so far); on ']' pop and append current × count. Handle multi-digit counts.

problems.title: Read N Characters Given read4 II - Call Multiple Times
problems.summary: You can only read a file through read4(buf4), which copies up to 4 characters into buf4 and returns how many it copied. Implement read(buf, n) that copies up to n characters into buf and returns the count. read may be called many times, so characters read4 fetched but you didn't return yet must be kept for the next call.
problems.idea: Keep a 4-char buffer + pointer + count as fields across calls; drain the buffer first, call read4 when empty, stop at n or EOF.

def read_calls(file, ns):
    _file["s"] = file; _file["p"] = 0
    s = Solution(); out = []
    for n in ns:
        buf = [""] * (n + 4)
        c = s.read(buf, n)
        out.append("".join(buf[:c]))
    return out

def _f0():

problems.title: LRU Cache
problems.summary: Design a fixed-capacity key-value cache with get(key) (returns -1 if missing) and put(key, value). When it's full, inserting a new key evicts the least recently used key. Both operations should be O(1).

problems.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) - Duplicates allowed
problems.summary: Design a multiset with average O(1) insert(val), remove(val) and getRandom(). insert returns true if val was not already present. remove deletes one copy and returns true if val was present. getRandom returns an element with probability proportional to how many copies it has.
problems.example: insert 1 → true, insert 1 → false, insert 2 → true, getRandom → 1 with prob 2/3
problems.idea: ArrayList of values + map val → Set of indices; remove by swapping with the last element and fixing its index set.

problems.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
problems.summary: Each node of a linked list has next and an extra random pointer (to any node, or null). Return a deep copy, where the new nodes point only to other new nodes.
problems.example: [[7,null],[13,0],[11,4],[10,2],[1,0]]  (value, index that random points to) → an identical, separate list
problems.idea: Map old → new in two passes; or interleave copies (A→A'→B→B') then split for O(1) space.
problems.py_post:
@@PYHELPERS@@

def RL(pairs):
    nodes = [Node(v) for v, _ in pairs]
    for i, n in enumerate(nodes):
        n.next = nodes[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(nodes) else None
        r = pairs[i][1]
        n.random = nodes[r] if r is not None else None
    return nodes[0] if nodes else None
def RA(head):
    nodes, n = [], head
    while n and len(nodes) < 100000:
        nodes.append(n); n = n.next
    idx = {id(x): i for i, x in enumerate(nodes)}
    return [[x.val, idx.get(id(x.random)) if x.random else None] for x in nodes]
def no_shared(a, b):
    seen, n = set(), a
    while n: seen.add(id(n)); n = n.next
    n = b
    while n:
        if id(n) in seen: return False
        n = n.next
    return True

def _f0():
    h = RL([[7,None],[13,0],[11,4],[10,2],[1,0]])
    c = Solution().copyRandomList(h)
    got = [RA(c), no_shared(h, c)]
    return got
_t('[[7,null],[13,0],[11,4],[10,2],[1,0]]', _f0, '[[[7,null],[13,0],[11,4],[10,2],[1,0]],true]', 'eq')
def _f1():
    h = RL([[1,1],[2,1]])
    c = Solution().copyRandomList(h)
    got = [RA(c), no_shared(h, c)]
    return got
_t('[[1,1],[2,1]]', _f1, '[[[1,1],[2,1]],true]', 'eq')
def _f2():
    got = RA(Solution().copyRandomList(None))
    return got
_t('empty list', _f2, '[]', 'eq')

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.summary: Are the two strings anagrams of each other?

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.summary: Ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters, is the string a palindrome?
problems.example: "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" → true

problems.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problems.summary: Return the longest substring that reads the same forwards and backwards.

problems.title: Palindromic Substrings
problems.summary: Count the substrings that are palindromes.

problems.title: Encode and Decode Strings
problems.summary: Design encode(list of strings) → one string, and decode(string) → the original list. Strings may contain any characters.

problems.title: Same Tree
problems.summary: Are two binary trees identical in shape and values?

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree
problems.summary: Mirror the tree (swap every node's left and right children).

problems.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problems.summary: A path is any sequence of connected nodes. Return the maximum path sum.

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.summary: Return the node values level by level, left to right.

problems.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
problems.summary: Design a way to turn a binary tree into a string and back.

problems.title: Subtree of Another Tree
problems.summary: Is subRoot identical to some subtree of root?

problems.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
problems.summary: Rebuild the tree from its preorder and inorder sequences (values are unique).

problems.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
problems.summary: Is the tree a valid BST (left subtree < node < right subtree, recursively)?

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
problems.summary: Return the k-th smallest value in a BST.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
problems.summary: Return the lowest node that has both p and q as descendants (a node counts as its own descendant).

problems.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
problems.summary: Implement insert(word), search(word) and startsWith(prefix).
problems.example: insert apple; search apple → true; search app → false; startsWith app → true

problems.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
problems.summary: Like a trie, but search patterns may contain '.', which matches any letter.

problems.title: Word Search II
problems.summary: Return every dictionary word that can be traced in the letter grid.

problems.title: Find Median from Data Stream
problems.summary: Support addNum(x) and findMedian() over a growing stream of numbers.
